definitions.explanation: Something that causes difficulty or is not favorable. Often used when a schedule, situation, or condition does not work well.
Something morally questionable or socially unacceptable. Often used in formal or business contexts for misconduct or scandalous behavior.

examples.japanese: {何|なに}か{不都合|ふつごう}がありますか。
その{日|ひ}は{不都合|ふつごう}なので、{別|べつ}の{日|ひ}にしましょう。
examples.english: That day is inconvenient, so let's choose another day.

examples.japanese: ご{不都合|ふつごう}な{点|てん}がございましたらお{知|し}らせください。
examples.english: Please let us know if there is anything inconvenient.

examples.japanese: {不都合|ふつごう}な{事実|じじつ}。
{彼|かれ}には{何|なに}か{不都合|ふつごう}なことがあるらしい。
examples.english: It seems he has something improper going on.

examples.japanese: {不都合|ふつごう}な{行為|こうい}が{発覚|はっかく}して、{辞任|じにん}に{追|お}い{込|こ}まれた。
examples.english: Improper conduct was discovered, and he was forced to resign.

notes:
Combines {不|ふ} (not) + {都合|つごう} (convenience, circumstances). Functions both as a na-adjective ({不都合|ふつごう}な) and as a noun ({不都合|ふつごう}がある). The word carries a slightly formal tone and is common in business and polite speech.

USAGE:
Sense 1 is straightforward — something is inconvenient or unsuitable. Sense 2 has a euphemistic quality: calling something {不都合|ふつごう} often implies wrongdoing or scandal without stating it directly, as in the common phrase {不都合|ふつごう}な{真実|しんじつ} (inconvenient truth).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {不都合|ふつごう}がある — there is an inconvenience
- {不都合|ふつごう}な{点|てん} — an inconvenient point
- {不都合|ふつごう}な{事実|じじつ} — an inconvenient fact
- ご{不都合|ふつごう} — inconvenience (polite)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {都合|つごう}が{悪|わる}い — inconvenient; the more colloquial way to express the same idea
- {不便|ふべん} — inconvenient; focuses on practical difficulty rather than suitability
